task_scope: One preserved failed-run receipt plus a caller-authored diagnosis and recovery proposal; gate evidence links, repeated identical attempts, permission/budget deltas, exact-signature verification, and stop conditions.

findings: The failure-case evidence gate checks prerequisites for claiming a reproduced implementation defect; it does not accept a bounded recovery plan or gate retry instructions.

The portable research episode validator checks caller-declared artifact versions, execution/run relations, reviews, omissions, and fork mappings; it does not connect a diagnosis and proposed recovery instruction to one failure signature or suppress an unchanged failed retry.

The governed improvement transition preflight checks aggregate predecessor/successor evaluator, quality, cost, failure, authority, rollback, and next-round declarations; it does not process one failed task run into evidence-linked recovery guidance.

The new tool retains the original failure, requires evidence-linked observations or labeled hypotheses, blocks missing verification/stops, unknown or expanded budgets, permission changes, and repeated unchanged failed actions, and emits only a human-review packet.

The real-task result is a single local preflight over caller-supplied public Actions evidence; it is not an outcome trial. Relative completion quality, reliability, operator effort, latency, and monetary cost remain unknown.
unique_remaining_use_cases: Preflight a specific proposed retry or recovery using preserved failure evidence, exact signature, labeled diagnosis, verification, and explicit stop rules without invoking it.
next_low_cost_comparison: If an actual recovery is separately approved and executed, compare the retained failure signature, verifier result, operator effort, and scope/permission effects against a manual review of the same failure. Do not claim performance or cost superiority from this single preflight.
